text:
alex: thinking through a dual-path approach where tiny fastpath requests skip the coalesce window but can optionally merge back into the main batcher for KV cache reuse. tradeoffs?

mira: sounds useful for reducing wasted cold KV work, but mergeback feels tricky. how do we prevent head-of-line blocking when a fastpath request lands mid-batch?

sam: one option: mergeback only at batch boundaries. fastpath outputs go to a small per-tenant buffer and get stitched into the next batch window. simpler but can add a tiny stall on the next batch.

alex: yeah. my worry is bursty tiny requests from many tenants causing the next batch to bloat and increase latency for long requests. we need admission/credit checks on mergeback.

tj: propose two signals: "mergeable" (boolean) and "merge_cost_est" (tokens). allow mergeback if tenant has merge_credits > merge_cost_est. credits refill with time-based budget. cheap to check.

chen: love the credit idea. also suggest a soft-evict hint: if batch is within latency SLO headroom < X ms, refuse mergeback. keeps long-tail SLOs safe.

caroline: +1. we should also consider KV-affinity tagging. if fastpath warmed the KV for a particular prefix, mergeback can join only batches with matching affinity to avoid cross-warm pollution.

alex: KV-affinity is good but requires batcher to expose affinity buckets. that's a surface change. how big of a refactor?

mira: moderate. current batcher groups by model+seqlen. add an affinity key is incremental, but we need eviction semantics: affinity buckets shouldn't starve others.

sam: operationally, metrics to track: mergeback_attempts, mergeback_accept_rate, added_tokens_per_batch, tail_latency_delta.post_merge. need dashboards and an alert if tail latency increases > 5% for 5m.

infra-bot: FYI: perf-test cluster "mergeback-canary" spun up (3 GPUs) by @caroline. logs at https://internal.redwood/infra/mergeback-canary

caroline: ran a quick sim overnight. mergeback helped reduce cold-KV misses by ~28% for low-latency paths, but increased p99 by ~6ms in peak windows.

alex: okay measurable. options: 1) conservative mergeback (credits + affinity + headroom guard), 2) full mergeback (more hits, more risk), 3) no mergeback (simpler).

tj: we should prototype conservative first. implement credits + headroom guard + small per-tenant merge queue. keep knobs in config: merge_enabled, credit_rate, headroom_threshold_ms, affinity_enabled.

mira: API/observable note: expose per-tenant merge credit and a small event stream when mergeback is rejected for SLO reasons. helps debugging customer reports.

chen: also add a telemetry tag on tokens that originated from mergeback so Optimize can attribute cost wins.

alex: agree. last question: preemption / cancellation semantics. if a merged request sits waiting and gets cancelled by client, do we remove it from merge queue or leave to avoid hole?

sam: remove it. leaving holes complicates packing logic and gives poor latency guarantees. cancellation should decrement credits only if actually executed; otherwise refund.

caroline: implementation note: keep merge queue bounded per-tenant to avoid memory amplification during DOS. e.g., max_merge_items = 50.

alex: timeline? can someone spike conservative prototype (batcher + credits + headroom guard) in next 2 weeks? low fidelity sim + perf-run would be enough.

tj: I can take prototype. will PR a sketch of the credit model and a proof-of-concept patch for the batcher merge hook by EOW.

mira: I'll help with metrics + dashboard wiring.

chen: I'll add a simple sim for affinity bucket collisions.

alex: great — thanks all. tagging this as follow-up for the continuous-batching refactor RFC. we'll review canary results before enabling in prod. :thumbsup:
